description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review) while restoring perl-tests/each.t's inline
`ok(1,'SKIP')` rows (task #965).  PRE-EXISTING.

THE ROWS (perl-tests/each.t 64 and 65, restored from upstream t/op/each.t):

    use feature 'refaliasing';
    no warnings 'experimental::refaliasing';
    $a = 7;                      # $a is the FILE LEXICAL declared at each.t:177
    my %h2;
    \$h2{f} = \$a;
    ($a, $b) = (each %h2);
    is "$a $b", "f 7", 'each in list assignment';      # PCL: ' 7'
    $a = 7;
    ($a, $b) = (3, values %h2);
    is "$a $b", "3 7", 'values in list assignment';    # PCL: ' 7'

perl 5.40.3 gives 'f 7' / '3 7'; PCL gives ' 7' / ' 7' -- $a comes out EMPTY,
$b is right.  A blank where a letter belongs: the #964 failure mode.

WHAT WAS RULED OUT (do not redo these -- all four PASS under PCL, byte-identical
to perl; scratch files in the s464ay worktree):
  p13b â the block verbatim with `our ($a,$b)`                    PASSES
  p38  â both variables `my` lexicals                             PASSES
  p39  â `my $a` declared far earlier, used, and captured by a sub PASSES
  p40  â the file's MIXED shape: `my $a` file lexical + package $b PASSES
So it is neither the feature, nor the aliasing itself, nor the lexical/package
mix, nor lexical distance.  Something ELSE in each.t is the trigger.

NEXT STEP IS A BISECTION, not another guess: take the restored
perl-tests/each.t, cut it down from the top keeping the final block, and find
the smallest prefix that still gives ' 7'.  Candidates visible in the file
between the declaration and the block: `my $a = byte_utf8a_to_utf8n(...)` at
line 177 gives $a a byte-string value; the file runs several `fresh_perl_like`
children; and `%u`/`%b` are iterated with `each`/`keys` in between.

WHY IT WAS INVISIBLE: the two rows carried an inline `ok(1, 'SKIP: use feature
refaliasing not supported in PCL')` whose comment said the feature was
"experimental, removed in Perl 5.40" and that "PCL does not implement
reference aliasing".  BOTH halves are false -- refaliasing is IMPLEMENTED
(docs/not-supported.md 'Ref aliasing (use feature refaliasing) â IMPLEMENTED
s396 (#325)', which even names this each.t block as an affected site) and the
feature is not removed.  The rows are restored and DELIBERATELY NOT
registered; they sit in baselines/fail-baseline.tsv with this task as cause.
subject: SILENT WRONG (in-file only): refaliasing `\$h2{f} = \$a` then `($a,$b) = (each %h2)` gives ' 7' instead of 'f 7' in perl-tests/each.t rows 64/65 -- FOUR isolated reproductions of the same shape all PASS, so the trigger is something else in the file; needs a bisection
